title: Responses fidelity bridge: audit and action plan for OpenAI Responses compatibility
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Perform a targeted audit of functional and behavioral differences between Redwood's core API event model and the OpenAI Responses API and produce a pragmatic translation/bridge design plus an implementation & canary plan. Focus areas: streaming chunk semantics, tool/function call handshake and finalization, structured JSON output schema fidelity, token provenance and stop/truncation behavior, and metadata/role mapping. Deliverables: gap catalog, lossiness scoring, a translation shim spec, contract tests, and a staged rollout with telemetry and guardrails.
acceptance_criteria: Gap catalog enumerates all observed delta cases with reproducible test vectors
A translation/shim spec exists with explicit rules for streaming chunk aggregation, tool-call begin/complete semantics, and structured-output reconciliation
Integration test suite (contract tests) that can run against both Redwood runtime and an OpenAI Responses mock verifies behavior for top 20 delta cases
Canary route implemented that translates OpenAI Responses calls to Redwood runtime for 1% of traffic with feature-flagging and observable loss metrics
Playbook for deterministic vs best-effort translation and for automatic fallback when lossiness > threshold
milestones: M1: Initial audit & reproducible test vectors (done)
M2: Lossiness taxonomy and scoring function (done)
M3: Translation/shim spec and API contract tests (in progress)
M4: Runtime shim prototype + unit tests
M6: Post-canary review and rollout decision

decisions: Adopt an in-process translation shim between the public Responses API surface and the Redwood runtime to minimize changes to runtime inetfaces
Streaming coalescing policy: default 150ms window with consumer-configurable max-chunk-join length to avoid head-of-line blocking

Tool/function-call model: always emit explicit begin/argument/complete events; when runtime can only stream partial args, buffer and synthesize a finalizing 'function_complete' event with provenance metadata
Structured-output validation: use a two-phase approach — (1) best-effort normalization for obvious shape differences, (2) enforce schema for strict mode with clear error codes
Lossiness threshold: automatic fallback to native Redwood API when lossiness_score >= 0.35 for a given request profile
risks: Runtime performance regression from buffering/coalescing in high-throughput paths
Edge cases causing mismatched ordering between streamed tokens and reconstructed tool-call arguments
False positives in lossiness scoring that lead to unnecessary routing changes
SDK/consumer reliance on subtle OpenAI-specific behaviors that cannot be replicated deterministically
Increased complexity in observability due to translated provenance headers and synthesized events
testing_plan: Unit tests for event translation rules (chunk aggregation, role mapping, newline normalization)
Contract tests that replay recorded OpenAI Responses sessions against translated path and compare semantic equivalence
Fuzz tests for structured-output reconciliation to surface schema-mangling cases
Load tests to measure latency and throughput impact with the translation shim enabled
Canary validation criteria: error rate <= baseline+0.5%, median p95 token-latency increase <= 12%, and lossiness_score distribution acceptable
rollout_plan: Feature-flag controlled rollout: off -> internal -> 1% public canary -> 10% -> ramp to 100% if metrics stable
Telemetry: lossiness_score histogram, synthesized-event-count per request, streaming-merge-duration distribution, toolcall-finalization-latency
Alerting: automatic rollback if error rate or user-facing deviations exceed thresholds
Migration docs and SDK compatibility notes for downstream consumers
Post-mortem and learning capture after each ramp stage
